channel.title: The Wilson Times - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Wilson Times (wilsontimes.com)

item.title: Dancers raise $20,500 for children’s home
item.description: Local dancers give back to the community by raising more than $20,000 for the Free Will Baptist Children's Home.

item.title: America is doing just fine, says MAGA
item.description: A guest columnist disputes MAGA’s claim that America is entering a ‘Golden Age,’ pointing to job losses, Gaza’s death toll, immigration abuses and expanding presidential power as evidence of a slide toward autocracy.

item.title: Thoughts on oligarchy, AI and the loss of an NC film icon
item.description: A policy analyst warns AI could upend white-collar America as trade and automation gutted manufacturing, enriching a billionaire oligarchy, and mourns “Dawson’s Creek” star James van der Beek, a devoted friend of North Carolina’s film industry.

item.title: New construction moderates home prices
item.description: As North Carolina struggles with rising home prices and an 80,000-unit housing shortfall, research shows new construction is key to affordability — despite local moves to limit building.

item.title: Rural public schools want access to opportunity, not handouts
item.description: Former Teacher of the Year Kimberly Jones, once a rural area public school student, says state lawmakers should offer the same opportunities to rural students that are offered to those from wealthier areas.

item.title: Our Opinion: Can Wilson top 22% turnout in 2026 primaries?
item.description: The Wilson Times' editorial page weighs Wilson County’s low primary turnout against past elections, outlines key sheriff, U.S. Senate and Congress primaries for both parties and urges residents to vote.

item.title: State of the Union response shows Dems aren’t working for you
item.description: A letter-writer argues that Democrats revealed at Trump’s State of the Union and in Abigail Spanberger’s response that they prioritize illegal immigrants and partisan attacks over policies that help American citizens.

item.title: Darryl Smith leaves indelible mark on Wilson
item.description: Wilson lawyer Darryl Gilliam Smith, a devoted civil rights advocate, festival organizer and Omega Psi Phi member who made helping others his calling, is remembered after his death at 74.

item.title: Sheriff: Road rage shooting deemed self-defense
item.description: Wilson County sheriff says no charges for driver who shot another motorist during a road rage crash on U.S. 264; DA rules 20-year-old acted in self-defense, with smart glasses video used in the investigation.
